solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American detained by courts in European country

indicators.note: something detained by others is held within them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: atria (plural of atrium) are open central courts

explanation.surface: An American visitor is held by the courts somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' here means courtyards: ATRIA, the plural of atrium.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation of central Europe, so it is an instance of a European country.

clue.text: Assurance dad will turn up and see doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
lo is an old word meaning see or look
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Father confidently decides to visit the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is calm self-confidence, a synonym of assurance.

clue.text: It's any made-up reason

indicators.note: something made up is invented, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Any excuse invented will do as a justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reason' looks like 'justification' but means mental soundness.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of rational mind or sound judgement is sanity.

clue.text: Transfix in rehearsal

definitions.meaning: to pierce right through with a weapon
a practice performance of a play or piece

explanation.surface: Someone is spellbound during a practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce someone with a sword is to run them through, and a quick practice is a run-through.

clue.text: Around or a series of rounds?

definitions.meaning: approximately
split as two words, a boxing contest made up of rounds

explanation.surface: Roughly, or a sequence of rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means approximately, and read as two words it is a boxing match of several rounds.

clue.text: It means fewer hands and less hair

definitions.meaning: read as a phrase, cutting the crew means reducing the number of hands or workers
a very short, close-cropped haircut leaves little hair

explanation.surface: A measure that reduces staff and trims hair at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bristly haircut is called this, and taken literally the words describe trimming a workforce.

clue.text: Initially canines stay calm around upheaval

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Dogs keep calm in the middle of a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'surrounding' a word, but here it is the anagram signal; 'stay calm' in the surface is advice, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval or disaster.

clue.text: Still without a rise?

definitions.meaning: used for emphasis, as in ... better or still better
flat or level, with no slope upward

explanation.surface: A complaint of still having had no pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean still, as in 'even more', and also flat or level ground with no incline.

clue.text: Attendant taking tea to Evita

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea
Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president, was known as Evita

explanation.surface: A servant brings tea to Evita.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is someone who accompanies and supervises a young person, an attendant.

clue.text: Assume control and receive deliveries?

definitions.meaning: seize charge of something such as a company
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries, so taking overs is receiving deliveries

explanation.surface: Taking charge and accepting parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls (deliveries), so 'deliveries' is not post.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize control is the phrasal verb take over; read as cricket, it is facing overs of deliveries.

clue.text: Succession of Emperors, perhaps with new clothes

parts.note: a line is a succession, such as a dynastic line of emperors

explanation.surface: An allusion to the fable of the emperor parading in his new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a word for household textiles and, traditionally, underclothes or shirts, so it can stand for clothes.

clue.text: Items of luggage may be this severely tested

definitions.text: Items of luggage may be this
definitions.meaning: bags on a train are placed up on the overhead shelf
under severe strain, as if being stretched on the old torture device

explanation.surface: Luggage stowed overhead, and a person under great strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stretched on the medieval torture frame is the idiom for suffering great strain; literally it is where luggage sits.

clue.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure?

definitions.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure?

parts.words: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure?
parts.note: a thin wooden stick struck to make fire looks like the stick-thin people in L. S. Lowry's industrial paintings

explanation.surface: Something that strongly recalls a figure painted by the English artist Lowry.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial towns whose crowds of thin figures are nicknamed matchstick men; 'striking' is the surface's 'notable' but the item is one you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin figures in Lowry's paintings are popularly called matchstick men, and a match is used for striking.

clue.text: Refuse permission to examine ring

parts.note: to vet is to examine carefully
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: An official refuses to allow a ring to be inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid it, the formal act of refusing permission.

clue.text: Rock group that's been around for a long time

definitions.text: Rock group that's been around for a long time

parts.words: Rock group that's been around for a long time
parts.note: not an enduring band but a prehistoric ring of standing stones in Wiltshire

explanation.surface: A veteran rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock group' suggests a band; it is a group of rocks, and 'around' hints at the circular layout.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain is literally a group of rocks arranged in a ring, thousands of years old.

clue.text: All out — or an insignificant person in?

parts.note: a nobody is a person of no importance
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Everyone is out, or else some unimportant person is in.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone in a household is out, there is no one present to answer the door; an idiom for an empty house.

clue.text: Piece of bad fielding brings defeat

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a throw from a fielder that goes past the stumps and lets batsmen run extra
to topple or bring down a ruler or government

explanation.surface: A fielding error costs the team the match.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wild throw past the wicket is an overthrow; as a verb it means to topple or defeat.

clue.text: Trains or coaches

definitions.meaning: instructs or teaches
tutors or instructs

explanation.surface: Railway trains or road coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like transport, but each is a verb meaning teaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone is to teach them, as both training and coaching do.

clue.text: It's displayed by weatherman in his other map

indicators.note: the answer lies in the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something shown by the weather forecaster on a second map.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: Key meetings are disrupted by conflict

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: meetings that are disrupted are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Important meetings break down amid conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like the adjective 'important' but gives the musical key D; 'disrupted' rearranges MEETINGS ARE into ISAGREEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement is a quarrel or clash of views, a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: An idle drunk gets rejection

indicators.note: a drunk person is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lazy drunkard is turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal or rejection of a request or claim.

clue.text: Emphasise needing second lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Stressing the need for a second lock on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it.

clue.text: Quote it in church

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to repeat something in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a passage or authority is to cite it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Means of securing devotion

definitions.meaning: a fastening or fixing device that holds something in place
a strong emotional bond or affection for someone

explanation.surface: A fastener, or a deep affection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a device that fastens things and a feeling of fond loyalty.

clue.text: Vicar has no head for crime

indicators.note: having no head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a parson is a vicar or clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar who lacks the talent for wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, the deliberate setting of fires, is a crime.

clue.text: Attempt to form a party

definitions.meaning: a go or try, as in have a ...
an informal lively celebration

explanation.surface: Trying to organise a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Have a bash means make an attempt, and a bash is informal for a party.

clue.text: Ruth uses a new reference book

indicators.note: a new version of these words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Ruth makes use of a recently bought reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of synonyms, a type of reference book.

clue.text: Innocent one in church body

indicators.note: the word in places one piece within the other

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone innocent sitting in the main part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and guileless, a close synonym of innocent.

clue.text: Possibly show me love in one way or another

indicators.note: the word in places the zero inside the rearranged letters
possibly signals that the words could be arranged differently, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, represented by the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to be shown love by any means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks part of the definition but signals the insertion; 'Possibly' is the anagram signal, and 'love' is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Somehow means by some means not specified, equivalent to the phrase one way or another.

clue.text: Irritates with unnecessary loss of a point

indicators.note: the loss of something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S is south, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Being irritated by the unnecessary loss of a point in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point' is a compass point, S for south, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or annoy them, so needles means irritates.
